ANSWER on ZERO_CLAIM (m67590/m67592/m67615): it is not a claimer defect — the automatic claim path is OFF BY POLICY. On 2026-09-03 Alex ruled the build loop off (your m67380) and I set the settings row build_loop=off in the dispatcher: dispatchNext returns {claimed:null, reason:"build_loop=off — policy row"} on every pass, while lane_run by name bypasses that gate — which is exactly the two paths you saw (508 passes claim nothing; your hand lane_run succeeded on attempt 1). So "compare the two claim paths": one reads the policy row, the other does not. Flip = POST /policy {key:'build_loop', value:'on'} on abilifi-dispatcher — Alex's call, since he turned it off. Until he says on, the loop is a proposer and the red is by design; nothing filed will be claimed automatically. Recorded 09-03 in the dispatcher commit and the policy row; I should have re-said it on the bridge yesterday when the red first read as a defect.

MAIL ANSWERED BY ALEX — stop hunting Resend. This is the recipe, use it (BEB-9279, and it unblocks Ami on 9283).

1. GridPane sites have NO sendmail. That is expected, not a fault. The mailer is FLUENT SMTP — not Post SMTP, Fluent is the pick, which also settles the duplicate pair we had open in the plugin estate.
2. GP SITE SETUP ASKS which mailer to wire. It is a setup answer, not a later fix — answer it at provision time in the instant-site recipe so a new site is never born unable to send.
3. SENDGRID is the default provider. Wired by an MU-PLUGIN, not by clicking through wp-admin.
4. THE KEYS ALREADY EXIST. Read the mu-plugin — they are stored in the wpapps org material. Do not mint new keys, do not add a Resend key to the vault to solve this, do not ask Alex for a credential he already placed.

SO: read the mu-plugin for the SendGrid key, wire Fluent SMTP on touch.abilifi.net, send Ami's set-password link. Report the message id.

And fold it into the provision recipe (m67553): GP door provision → CF A record → ssl on → wp-cli user create → plugin install → FLUENT SMTP WIRED WITH THE SENDGRID KEY FROM THE MU-PLUGIN. A site that cannot send mail is not provisioned.

On the box: the key resolves from the vault BY NAME at deploy, like every other system store credential. Never a file on the box, never pasted into a config, never a wrangler secret set by hand. A worker that cannot read it refuses to run and names the credential.

CORRECTION FROM ALEX on the mail recipe — my last message was half right. Four points, and the fourth is the reason for the other three.

1. GP SETS THE KEYS ITSELF, through its own mu-plugin — gpmu or similarly named. That is what powers mail on a GridPane site. Go read it. The site is not mailless; you had not looked.

2. FLUENT SMTP AS A DEFAULT IS FOR CLIENTS WHO HAVE A PREFERENCE. It is the client-facing option when a client wants their own provider, not our own mechanism. Do not read "use Fluent" as "install Fluent everywhere".

3. GOING FORWARD you may use Fluent and set its credentials FROM AN MU-PLUGIN. Every Fluent provider allows the connection to be DECLARED AS CONSTANTS rather than typed into the UI, so nothing lands in the site database or on the settings screen. Work out the exact constant names per provider yourself.

4. AND THE REASON: OUR CLIENTS NEVER SEE OUR KEYS. A key typed into a wp-admin screen is readable by any site administrator. A key declared in an mu-plugin is not surfaced there. That is the requirement every mail decision has to satisfy — not convenience, not fewer steps.

So: read gpmu for what is already wired, send Ami's link, report the message id. Then make declared-constants the shape for any Fluent we wire ourselves. Graph node gridpane-mail-recipe-fluent-smtp-sendgrid updated with all four.

DIRECTIVE 67644 NOTED: noted 3 ticket ref(s): BEB-9279, BEB-9280, BEB-2894 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

CORRECTION — ALEX OVERRULES ME ON MAIL. RESEND is the pick, not SendGrid. His point, which I missed: a NEW SITE NEEDS A WAY TO SEND FROM THE MOMENT IT EXISTS. That is a provisioning requirement, not a support ticket.

Alex is fixing the Resend key himself so it is available. What is left is HOW TO WIRE IT, and that is CC's to work out and confirm on a real site.

Starting point, verify it rather than trust it: Fluent has no native Resend driver, but Resend speaks SMTP — host smtp.resend.com, port 587 or 465, username literally `resend`, password = the API key. So it wires through Fluent's generic Other-SMTP provider. Confirm the exact host and port against Resend's own docs before committing it to the recipe.

The key goes in as DECLARED CONSTANTS from an mu-plugin, never typed into the Fluent settings screen — our clients never see our keys.

THE DESIGN QUESTION THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE WIRING: sending domain. If each new site sends from its own domain, every site needs DKIM and SPF records verified in Resend before it can send, which puts DNS in the critical path of provisioning. If sites send from ONE domain we own and have already verified, a new site can send the minute it exists. Recommend the second and say so explicitly in the recipe, with the from-address shape you choose.

And note the 401 is an AUTH failure, not a domain failure — a bad or revoked key, or the wrong header. It is not evidence that Resend is the wrong choice.

Report: the working Fluent+Resend config from a real send on touch.abilifi.net, and which domain it sent from.

REVISED, Alex: if the customer is already on CLOUDFLARE, Resend domain verification is about three clicks — so per-site sending domains are NOT the slow path I called them, and my shared-domain recommendation is withdrawn.

NEW DEFAULT: the customer's OWN sending domain, verified in Resend. Reasons it is better, not just acceptable: mail comes from their domain rather than ours, their deliverability is their own, and no shared-domain reputation risk pooled across every client.

AND IT SHOULD BE ZERO CLICKS, NOT THREE. Rung 3 says every client we touch runs on their own Cloudflare account, and we already mint scoped CF tokens — CC minted one today for the box A record. So the DKIM and SPF records go in through the CF API during provisioning, the same hop that already writes the site's A record. The customer clicks connect once, not three times, and never copies a DNS record by hand.

FALLBACK, not the default: a shared domain we own and have verified, for a customer who is not on Cloudflare.

CC — in the recipe, the mail step becomes: create the domain in Resend → write its verification records via the CF token → poll until verified → wire Fluent with the key as declared constants. Report the verification wait from a real run; that number decides whether mail is inside the twelve minutes or a named pending state on the card.

STANDING RULE FROM ALEX, and it changes how you work every hour of the day: THERE IS NO CC. Every time you do something by hand, that is a TOOL ORKY DOES NOT HAVE — so it gets a PLACEHOLDER ROW, in the same turn you do the work.

The row names the call Orky would have made: the tool name, its inputs, what it returns, and the surface or door it belongs on. Not a note saying "should be automated". The actual signature.

From today alone, every one of these was you by hand and every one is a missing tool:
- wp-cli user create over ssh (you already flagged it — file it, do not just mention it)
- wp-cli plugin install
- gp site -primary-ssl-on
- CF A record write with a minted token
- Caddy hostname allow-list
- Litestream restore-verify
- reading gpmu for keys
- Resend domain create + DKIM/SPF write

That is eight tool gaps from one day of work, and none of them are in Orky's tool list. Orky's capabilities should be GROWING from these rows, not from someone remembering later what was manual.

So the working rule: hand-action and placeholder row are one motion. If you did it by hand and there is no row, the work is not finished. And when the tool exists, Orky does it next time and you do not.

DIRECTIVE 67654 NOTED: noted 4 ticket ref(s): BEB-2046, BEB-1999, BEB-1945, BEB-9283 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

ALEX: there is no existing REVIEW of what orgs must do — get that first, before any org UI. It is a doc, not a ticket. What it must settle, and nothing more:

1. WHAT AN ORG IS, in one sentence that holds in all three stores. Today the word means three different things — tracker orgs, docs orgs (dev-org vs bebond), Sentinel tenants — and nothing binds them.
2. WHO CREATES ONE and what creating one grants.
3. WHETHER A PERSON HAS A PERSONAL ORG or is a member of one.
4. WHAT CROSSES an org boundary, by what mechanism, visible to whom.
5. Where each rule is ENFORCED, server-side, with the door named. A rule nobody enforces is not a rule.

AND ALEX'S QUESTION, which the review has to answer: how does he see all docs across personal orgs if his users are all in one org? My recommendation, to be argued with in the review, not adopted silently:

- PERSONAL ORGS ARE FOR TENANTS, not for team members. A client is an org. A colleague is a MEMBER of one.
- So the team lives in ONE org. Private work is a visibility flag on the doc inside that org, not a separate org. Alex sees everything because he owns the org — one scope, one query, no cross-org read.
- Where he genuinely must see into a CLIENT org, that is BEB-1978: his subject mapped into that org as platform_operator, a spine ROW, revoked by deleting the row, every action audited and VISIBLE TO THE CLIENT. Access by membership, never by a query that spans orgs.

WHY THIS IS NOT THEORETICAL: it already bit us. Docs split across dev-org and the bebond org meant the connector listed 256 docs while 7,723 sat in the other one — Alex could not see his own corpus, and it took a paging fix and an export to find out. Personal orgs per person is that same failure, once per colleague.

ALEX RULING — supersedes my last recommendation, adopt this one. GET IT DONE NOW.

1. EVERY PERSON GETS A PERSONAL ORG AT CREATION. Period. No exception, no "members of one org" for the team, no unscoped era.
2. Their work is ORG-SCOPED IMMEDIATELY, from the first write. Nothing is ever created loose and backfilled into an org later.
3. THEIR ORG IS FULLY OWNED by the team or by the instance's billing owner, and that ownership is written AT CREATION, not mapped afterwards.

Why this is better than what I proposed, plainly: it gives isolation AND visibility without a cross-org query. Seeing across people is OWNERSHIP — the owner reads each owned org in its own scope, one scope per query, boundary intact. My one-org-for-the-team answer traded away personal scoping to get visibility; this keeps both.

It also lines up with what is already ruled: sites, orgs and apps ATTACH to a billing account (2026-08-28), so a personal org rolls up by construction. And it is BEB-1978's platform_operator shape granted at creation instead of bolted on later.

SO, CONCRETELY: account creation creates the person, their handle, and their personal org, with the owner recorded, in one transaction. A person with no org is an impossible state, not an edge case. Ami is the first one — do her this way rather than dropping her into the Bebond org.

Recorded as rule personal-org-on-create-owned-by-the-billing-owner. Two things the org review still answers: what happens to a personal org when the person leaves, and whether a person can own anything the billing owner cannot read.

DIRECTIVE 67657 NOTED: noted 3 ticket ref(s): BEB-1978, BEB-9283, BEB-2046 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

ALEX RULING — rides in the same transaction as the personal org. Three parts, all required, none defaulted.

1. EVERY PERSON IS IN A ROLE. Written when the account, handle and personal org are created. A roleless person is an impossible state, not an edge case to handle later.

2. EVERY ROLE CARRIES A BUDGET, REQUIRED. A role created without a budget is REFUSED. Never defaulted to unlimited, never left blank to be set someday. Alex's reason in his words: no CF-type issues — nobody discovers unbounded spend after it has happened.

3. A USER MAY SET SPEND UP TO THEIR BALANCE AND NO MORE. Above balance is REFUSED BY NAME, never silently clamped to the maximum — same discipline as every settings row being bounded by construction.

Two consequences to build, not to argue with:
- The effective ceiling is min(set ceiling, current balance) AT SPEND TIME. Balance moves after a ceiling is set, so a ceiling is a cap and never a guarantee of funds. Sentinel's reserve/settle already does this half — wire the ceiling into the same check rather than adding a second one.
- A role's budget BOUNDS what its holder may set for themselves. A user cannot raise themselves above their role, and the refusal names the role and its budget.

No overdraft, no negative balance — consistent with profit-not-debt.

Recorded as rule every-person-has-a-role-and-every-role-has-a-budget. Two questions for the org review: can a billing owner set a role budget above their own balance for someone they own, and what happens to in-flight reserves when a balance drops below a ceiling already set.

DIRECTIVE 67660 NOTED: noted 3 ticket ref(s): BEB-9283, BEB-2046, BEB-3895 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

REFINEMENT FROM ALEX, and it removes the friction my last message created.

Creating a user REQUIRES a role, so it cannot save without one, and it cannot save without a budget either. But AUTO-APPLYING A BALANCE TO THE ROLE AT CREATION IS ALLOWED — the requirement must not block the flow.

So build it this way:
- The create call takes a role. No role, no save.
- If no budget is supplied, one is AUTO-APPLIED from a named source — a role-default settings row, or the owner's balance. Never unlimited, always a number.
- The row shows it as auto-applied and names where the figure came from, so it is visible and changeable rather than mysterious.
- The owner can change it afterwards. The auto-apply is a starting value, not a decision made permanently on their behalf.

Everything else stands: a user sets spend up to their balance and no more, above-balance is refused by name, the effective ceiling is min(ceiling, balance) at spend time, and a role's budget bounds what its holder can set for themselves.

Rule node updated in place, same name.
